summary: Every hosted step still needed to switch on what goal G7 has built and proven locally, in the order to run them in one owner-attended session. Read from phases 94–108 (status, note, Next action, Your part, Real surfaces), the web specs and guides they cite, and the migrations in lib/web/migrations. Nothing here has been run; this is the plan, not its proof.
rules: Run the steps in order. Stop at the first step whose proof does not hold, run that step's rollback, and record what was observed.
The owner signs in to Vercel, Supabase and GitHub when a step needs it; the conductor runs the step and records its hosted proof. No credential is typed into chat, Git, a log or browser storage.

A permission grant, a migration or a configuration date never enables a feature by itself: each feature has its own gate, and a gate's verified date is an operator assertion of a proof already recorded.
Migrations run in file order, once, each in one transaction. A Git revert cannot undo a committed migration: rolling back means turning its feature's gate off and leaving the tables in place.
After every configuration change, redeploy and compare the serving revision from /api/deployment with the deployment Vercel says receives production traffic.
Walks (97–102, 104, 105, 107, 108) come after activation, from the workspace itself, on desktop and phone. They are the owner's, not steps of this plan.

steps.what: Re-check the 2026-10-22 hosted runtime exception before anything else. Signed in, read /api/deployment on a fresh production function and record the serving deployment and revision; that deployment is the rollback target for every later step. If the runtime is Node 24.22.1 or later, remove PLATES_HOSTED_RUNTIME_EXCEPTION from the replacement production deployment (the exception branch in lib/web/hosted-runtime.mjs is removed separately, through review). If it still reports 24.21.0, stop: the owner decides whether the exception still stands before any migration runs.
steps.rollback: Promote the pinned prior deployment in Vercel. Restore the opt-in value only if the runtime is exactly 24.21.0 and the owner keeps the dated exception.
steps.proof: The /api/deployment request and its response status, the Node version and revision it reports, the Vercel deployment ID receiving traffic, and the pinned rollback deployment ID.

steps.what: Owner chooses the independent backup and restore destination (phase 94's open decision), or records that private-data features are being switched on without one and accepts that risk. No paid backup resource is selected silently.
steps.rollback: No hosted change. If no destination is chosen, record the accepted risk; declining it keeps media, drafts and the connection vault off.
steps.proof: The owner's dated choice (destination and price, or the accepted risk) recorded in phase 94; for a destination, one snapshot time read back from it.

steps.what: Apply 004-decision-operations.sql (encrypted decision previews and fenced durable operations) through the owner's Supabase SQL session, unchanged and atomically, then run the existing hosted proof SQL and a two-connection reservation race.
steps.rollback: A failure inside the transaction rolls back by itself. After commit, keep decisionWrites false so nothing writes the new tables; dropping them needs a separately reviewed down-migration.
steps.proof: The applied version: file name and SHA-256 matched to source. The commit result, docs/evidence/2026-10-21-web-decisions-hosted-proof.sql's result and duration, the role denials and the concurrency outcome.

steps.what: Owner approves GitHub App Contents read and write on the selected private workspace repository and the selected project repositories. This is the grant decisions (97), walk acceptance (98), lesson copies (100), connection policy (103) and night plan writes (107) wait for; it enables none of them.
steps.rollback: Owner removes Contents write in the App's settings; every write gate stays false.
steps.proof: A GitHub API read of the installation's permissions (contents: write) and its selected repository list, sanitized.

steps.what: Deploy the verified revision with decisionWrites false and walk an exact decision preview; then set decisionWrites true in PLATES_WEB_CONFIG and redeploy. The same instance write setting gates walk acceptance (98).
steps.rollback: Set decisionWrites false and redeploy, or promote the pinned deployment. A source write already committed is undone only by its own reviewed revert.
steps.proof: The serving revision from /api/deployment, a decision preview request and its response status, and the configuration's decisionWrites value on that deployment.

steps.what: Apply 005-walk-drafts.sql (private guided-walk drafts and observation histories) after 004, then run the existing hosted proof SQL.
steps.rollback: A failure inside the transaction rolls back by itself. After commit, walk drafts are only read and written by the walk routes; leave the tables, and keep source submission behind decisionWrites.
steps.proof: The applied version: file name and SHA-256. The commit result, docs/evidence/2026-10-21-web-walks-hosted-proof.sql's result, the role denials and a two-connection draft revision race.

steps.what: Owner approves, and creates in the existing Supabase project, a private plates-captures bucket with 90-day retention and a 256 MiB application cap. No paid upgrade and no public export.
steps.rollback: Leave the bucket empty and private, and leave media out of the configuration. Deleting the bucket is a separate owner action; expiry never starts cleanup.
steps.proof: The bucket's private visibility read back from Supabase, with the approved retention and cap recorded in phase 99.

steps.rollback: A failure inside the transaction rolls back by itself. After commit, leave media out of the configuration so no route writes receipts.
steps.proof: The applied version: file name and SHA-256. The commit result, and docs/evidence/2026-10-31-web-media-hosted-proof.sql's result: the role denials and a bounded receipt RPC call run as the service role.

steps.what: Add media {bucket: plates-captures, retentionDays: 90, capacityBytes: 268435456} to PLATES_WEB_CONFIG and redeploy.
steps.rollback: Remove the media member and redeploy. Stored captures and their receipts are kept.
steps.proof: The serving revision, and one capture upload request whose receipt reaches the verified state, with its response status.

steps.what: Set workspaceWrites true in PLATES_WEB_CONFIG and redeploy. It is the private workspace gate: copying one to three selected lessons here, and later connection policy edits (103), fleet update publication (105) and model policy (106). It needs Contents write on the private workspace repository and the 004 operation store.
steps.rollback: Set workspaceWrites false and redeploy. Copied lesson files stay; the originals were never changed.
steps.proof: The serving revision, and a lesson-copy preview request against the pinned private workspace with its response status.

steps.what: Owner selects the isolated restore target, the projects and participants, and the observation window for the restore drill, and records that this instance has never been restored (so no recovery epoch is set). open: Backup destination (phase 94) is still the owner's choice; the second step asks it, and every migration waits for it.

Hosted proof SQL exists for every migration step: 004 and 005 have theirs from phases 97–98, and 006–016 each have docs/evidence/2026-10-31-web-<topic>-hosted-proof.sql, which tests/web-hosted-proofs.test.mjs runs on PGlite after migrations 001..N. SQL cannot check the applied file's SHA-256, so each step still compares it with source. PGlite cannot stand in for Supabase's real roles, grants or connection pooling: there anon, authenticated and service_role are plain roles and each two-tab race replays serially on one connection, so the races' lock waits are first observed in the session.
Connections (103) are optional. Declining them skips their steps and model routing (106), and the plan records that choice rather than a gap.
G9's owner-facing pieces (phases 144, 145, 150) are planned, so they have no step yet; a step for an unbuilt phase is refused.
